Rent vs. Buy in Southern California: What Nobody Tells You

The Real Math Behind One of the Biggest Financial Decisions You Will Ever Make

By Rudy Corona · February 5, 2026

The Question That Keeps People Up at Night

Renting in Southern California is expensive; a two-bedroom often runs $2,200 to $3,500 per month, and rent goes up every year. Home prices and rates have made mortgage payments larger. Is buying still worth it in SoCal, or is renting smarter? I want to give you the honest answer, not a push into a decision.

What You Get When You Pay Rent

You get housing. You do not pay for major repairs. You can move more freely. But rent does not build equity, does not appreciate, and is not fixed. Rent in SoCal has increased 4% to 6% per year. A $2,500 apartment today can be $3,200 in five years — with nothing to show for it.

What You Get When You Pay a Mortgage

The principal portion reduces your loan balance every month. You are buying an ownership stake in an asset that in SoCal has historically appreciated 4% to 7% annually. Over 5 or 10 years, equity and appreciation can add up to hundreds of thousands of dollars in net worth versus renting.

The Calculation Most People Get Wrong

Comparing today's rent to today's mortgage and stopping there ignores two things: (1) Rent keeps going up; your fixed-rate payment does not. (2) You are comparing paying someone else to paying yourself. The true comparison is mortgage minus equity buildup and appreciation versus rent. For anyone planning to stay in SoCal 5+ years, the math often favors buying.

When Renting Makes Sense

Renting can be right for now if you will move in 2–3 years, if you are not financially ready, or if you have a below-market rental and need flexibility. As a permanent plan, renting means giving away income every month with no equity, no appreciation, no tax benefit.

The Honest Bottom Line

SoCal is expensive. Home prices have appreciated through recessions and rate spikes. The people who bought anyway are almost always glad they did. The best time to buy was ten years ago. The second best is as soon as you are genuinely ready. Find out if you are ready — free consultation, Rudy Corona, Corona Lending Group.
